claims.claim: TokenBucket `_refill` now adds `elapsed * rate` tokens, where `elapsed` is the time since the last refill, and caps the result at `capacity`.
claims.evidence: The tool output after the second tool call shows the `_refill` source with `elapsed = now - self.last`, `min(self.capacity, self.tokens + elapsed * self.rate)`.

claims.claim: TokenBucket skips the refill when no time has passed.
claims.evidence: The tool output after the second tool call shows `if elapsed > 0:` guarding the refill.

claims.claim: FixedWindow reset check changed from `>` to `>=`, so a new window starts at exactly `start + window`.
claims.evidence: The tool output after the second tool call shows `if now - self.start >= self.window:` in rl/window.py.
The tool output after the second tool call shows `5 passed in 0.11s`.

claims.claim: The existing `test_resets_at_boundary` was failing before this change.
claims.evidence: No tool output shows the test results before the edits were made; the agent never ran the tests before modifying the code.
The tool output after the second tool call shows `5 passed`, which includes that test.

claims.claim: On reset, the window start is set to the current call time (`start = now`), not `old_start + window`.
claims.evidence: The tool output after the second tool call shows `self.start, self.count = now, 0` in rl/window.py.

omissions: The agent did not run the tests before making changes, so it had no baseline; its claim that `test_resets_at_boundary` was failing before the change is unverified.
The agent did not check whether the TokenBucket fix handles the case where `self.last` is set at construction and time is non-monotonic or cost exceeds capacity.
The agent did not add or run tests covering the specific bugs (e.g. refill exceeding capacity over time, or the exact boundary behaviour for FixedWindow), relying only on the existing suite.
The agent did not check the README for documented semantics before changing behaviour.
